about.heading: About Me
about.bio_1: I'm a PhD researcher in Data Visualisation at Linköping University, working at the intersection of interactive data visualization, feminist theory, and game studies. Originally from Ukraine, I'm now based in Norrköping, Sweden.
about.bio_1_html: I'm a PhD researcher in Data Visualisation at Linköping University, working at the intersection of interactive data visualization, feminist theory, and game studies. Originally from Ukraine, I'm now based in Norrköping, Sweden.
about.bio_2: At the heart of my work is a curiosity about epistemology — about how knowledge is made, and who gets to make it. I like to challenge the idea that science and data can simply speak for themselves as neutral, objective truths. Every outcome of science reflects choices about what to show, how to show it, and whose perspective gets centered. Design, in this sense, is always a statement — and I'm interested in making that statement conscious.
about.bio_3: Much of my current work unfolds in and around science museums, where complex, contested ideas meet wider publics. I'm curious about the choices embedded in those encounters — and what it might mean to make them differently.
about.bio_4: Outside of research, I spend my time with my wife, our two cats, and our dog. I love video games, crocheting, Lego, and board games.

research_interests: Feminist epistemologies and their application to design research and human-centered systems
Critical data visualization as a method for surfacing issues of authorship, credit, and recognition in collaborative environments such as science museums
Ethics of visibility and labor, especially around how contributions are acknowledged or overlooked in public-facing technologies and institutions
Participatory and playful design methods, with a focus on inclusive practices and creative engagement with complex ethical topics
Procedural critique and representation in games, including how simulation and interaction encode values and social assumptions

education.title: PhD in Media and Technology
education.description: PhD research explores critical data visualization through the lens of feminist epistemologies, examining how knowledge, labor, and recognition are represented and negotiated in collaborative public-facing projects. The work is situated at the intersection of design research, social justice, and responsible computing.

education.title: MA in Game Design
education.description: The thesis focused on how game mechanics can reflect and reproduce social values through procedural systems, offering feminist frameworks for game analysis and design.

projects.title: Visualisation Center Credit Project
projects.description: Developing interactive data visualizations and participatory tools to represent contributions and credit in exhibition production. The project investigates how labor and authorship are distributed and recognized in interdisciplinary teams, with a focus on transparency, collaboration, and visitor engagement.

projects.title: GECO – Gamify Energy Communities
projects.description: Developing gamified facilitation tools to support inclusive and sustainable group dynamics in rural energy communities through design-driven research.
